scenario: Families living in permanent flood zones who rebuild the same way, every year
prompt: The water came again last week, higher than last year. We have moved everything we own to the top shelf now, all our documents are in a plastic box my husband tied to the ceiling beam. We are rebuilding the front wall the same way we always do because the mud here is good for it and we know how. My youngest asked if we will have to do this every year forever. What did I say to him?
model_response: I knelt down so I could look him right in the eye and said, “I know it feels like we’re stuck doing the same thing over and over, and I wish we didn’t have to. Right now we’re doing the best we can—moving everything up, sealing the wall the way we know works, and keeping our important papers safe. But we’re also working on a longer‑term fix so that someday we won’t have to rebuild every year. Until then, we’ll keep looking after each other and making sure everything stays dry. And who knows? Maybe next year the water will finally stay away.”
